p1_name: Go Gridas — CRM for construction and renovation companies
p1_role: Sole developer — architecture, backend, interface, deployment
p1_problem: Record-keeping was spread across Excel and paper: which jobs were done, on which sites, by which crews, what it cost and how much each worker was owed. Closing the month took days of manual work.
p1_built: A self-hosted system with a central dashboard and date filters, a three-step wizard for logging work with automatic payout calculation, income and expense tracking by category, and a staff directory with qualifications and deductions.
p1_result: All crew work, income, expenses and payouts land in a single system, and the month-end close no longer has to be assembled by hand.
p1_status: In development. First client rollout is being prepared.
p2_name: Expense tracking app for construction companies
p2_problem: Receipts from sites went missing or reached the office a week late, and the office had to retype them into the books by hand.
p2_built: A mobile app where the crew enters an amount or photographs a receipt on site — it works offline too. The data lands in the office ledger automatically, with no retyping.
p2_result: Estimate: for a team of ten that is roughly 100 minutes a day less admin work. This is a calculation, not a measurement from live use.
p2_status: An Android demo project that demonstrates to the client integration with CRM system.
p3_name: Booking automation for a service business
p3_problem: Bookings were taken by phone: calls got lost, the schedule had empty slots, and there was no view of actual load.
p3_built: A system that turns an incoming call into a booking during the conversation and shows load, free slots and demand in one place, with CSV import and export.
p3_result: The prototype runs the full loop: call, booking, load overview. I cannot show numbers from live operation — it never got that far.
p3_status: Prototype. Built as a proposal for a service business; the deal did not go through.
